ABC News, live updates 19 November 2026

SharePresident Donald Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

ABC News will have special coverage of the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting led by "World News Tonight" anchor David Muir, who will be anchoring from Shenzhen, China, across programs and platforms.

Muir will anchor "World News Tonight" from China on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and Thursday, Nov. 19.

Chief White House correspondent Mary Bruce and White House correspondent Karen Travers will also be reporting from China.

See the most recent developments below.

'We're choosing a different course,' Trump says of Xi, PutinAt the start of his trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, President Donald Trump said the three leaders have "a special responsibility to maintain open, respectful, and productive dialog on issues impacting not just our people but the entire planet."

"Too often, past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements, and we feel the opposite, and we think that we are sure about that," Trump said.

China's President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin arrive for a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong province, on Nov. 19, 2026.Doug Mills/POOL/AFP via Getty Images"No problems were ever solved under the old school refusing to talk about them. No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech. Together, we are choosing a different course," he added.

Trump said the summit "offers us the chance to seek out new opportunities, approaches on a range of very important issues, most of them, everybody in this room knows, and hopefully to create a better future for all of us."

President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin take part in a trilateral meeting with China's President Xi Jinping at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov. 19, 2026.Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty ImagesTrump said the leaders would discuss "all of the problems that are really being discussed in the world," including the conflict with Iran and the war in Ukraine.

Trump thanked both Xi and Putin, underscoring the historic nature of their meeting.

China's President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump and Russia's President Vladimir Putin leave after posing for photos before a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong province, on Nov. 19, 2026.Doug Mills/POOL/AFP via Getty ImagesThe president signaled his eagerness to discuss denuclearization, though recognized it is "a very hard thing" to accomplish.

"As the world's three largest nuclear powers by far, the United States, Russia, and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth, and also to lessen the risk that those weapons will ever be used," he said.

Trump also hit out at the International Criminal Court, which he said "has gotten out of control, which I believe we all agree has really strayed far from beyond its jurisdiction."

Trump-Xi-Putin meeting beginsPresident Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin began their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday.

China's President Xi Jinping (C), US President Donald Trump (R) and Russia's President Vladimir Putin (L) take part in a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov. 19, 2026.Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty ImagesPresident Donald Trump takes part in a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on Nov. 19, 2026.Mandel Ngan/AFP via Getty ImagesThe three leaders gathered around a circular table at the Kylin Villa for the talks -- the first ever such meeting between the leaders of the three nations.

Trump praises 'my friend' Xi ahead of trilateral meetingMeeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping ahead of their trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday, President Donald Trump expressed optimism that something "will come out" of their historic summit, pointing to a joint desire to see progress in Ukraine.

"It's been an incredible meeting," the president said. "I think something will come out. We're looking to both help with respect to the war with Russia and Ukraine."

China's President Xi Jinping walks with US President Donald Trump as they meet for a bilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong province, on Nov. 19, 2026.Doug Mills/POOL/AFP via Getty ImagesThe president spoke shortly after his one-on-one meeting with Putin, which Trump said "set the stage" for the planned trilateral meeting.

The president also touted his close relationship with Xi, saying, "You're my friend, and we have a very special relationship. I think as long as you and I are in charge of things we'll never have a problem."

President Donald Trump speaks with China's President Xi Jinping after leaders posed for a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, November 19, 2026.Greg Baker/Pool/AFP via Getty ImagesTrump said his visit to Shenzhen had "been amazing." He added, "From the very first state visit I made to China, all the way back in 2017, to this trip nine years later, President Xi and I have formed an outstanding personal relationship. It really is. Some people are unhappy when they hear that, but I'm very happy about it."

-ABC News' Fritz Farrow, Nicholas Kerr and Michelle Stoddart

Trump teases meeting with Putin and Xi, rejects AI regulationPresident Donald Trump touted his upcoming meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in his remarks at the APEC Leaders' Plenary Session in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday.

“I look forward to a historic trilateral meeting with President Xi and President Putin later today to discuss more opportunities for all three. So we look forward to that,” Trump told the leaders in the room.

President Donald Trump attends a meeting during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026.Ng Han Guan/Pool/EPA/Shutterstock

Trump also asserted that the U.S. would reject any form of what he called “globalist regulation” to “control or stifle” the development of frontier AI models -- saying that Americans invented the technology and that it should be cherished.

AI and potential regulation for the technology has been a headline global issue as models have continued to develop at breakneck paces, even as some tech leaders have warned of dire consequences if research moves too quickly. Trump has repeatedly rejected any form of official regulation over frontier AI models, insisting that the U.S.’s current laws go far enough.

President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping arrive for the plenary meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026.Ng Han Guan/Pool via AP

“It's superintelligence," he said, using his preferred terminology. "But we have to watch it. We have to be careful. We have to cherish it. It's almost completely good, but it's got some bad elements, and we have to be very careful in managing those bad elements."

President Donald Trump speaks during a meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026.Ng Han Guan/Pool via AP

In his remarks, Trump also touted the U.S.’s Alaska LNG pipeline, saying that he was working with multiple APEC countries to expand energy cooperation, and previewed future trade agreements, though he gave no specifics about which nations or what any of the terms of those deals might be.

-ABC News' Michelle Stoddard, Fritz Farrow and Nicholas Kerr

President Donald Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings with global leaders and for his second visit to China for a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
